summary.tldr: Amends the National Housing Strategy Act to address homeless encampments on federal land, Indigenous participation, and reporting on the strategy’s results.
what_it_does: Adds definitions for federal land, homeless encampment, and Indigenous peoples in the National Housing Strategy Act.
Requires the National Housing Strategy to include measures to prevent removing homeless encampments on federal land and to identify alternatives after meaningful engagement with residents.
Requires the Strategy to include processes for the active involvement and support of Indigenous peoples in housing programs that affect them, and for responses to respect their rights.
Requires the minister, when setting these measures and processes, to consult provincial housing ministers and work with organisations that represent Indigenous peoples.
Expands the triennial report to include success metrics, plus longitudinal data broken down by groups, including Indigenous peoples and other groups named in the Act.
Requires the minister to monitor how housing policy affects vulnerable groups, Indigenous peoples, people with housing need, and people who have experienced homelessness.
summary.background: The bill amends the National Housing Strategy Act. It adds new requirements for the National Housing Strategy and for the report on its effectiveness.
